title: Card sets and expansions
summary: TCG Card Shop Simulator groups its cards into named expansions and into separate border finishes, so a collection is tracked by set and by look rather than as one long list of cards.
body: Cards belong to expansions. The game keeps a fixed list of expansion names instead of letting a set be anything at all, which is why cards from different sets can sit in the same binder and still be different cards.

A card also has a finish. Border styles are their own fixed list, running from the plain base look through first editions, silver, gold, EX and the full-art border, and the game ships a border image for each one rather than drawing them on the fly.
The two are tracked separately. A card's expansion and a card's border are recorded independently, which is why one set can hold both a plain card and a special finish of that same card.

Set and finish both feed price changes. The list of things the game lets move a card's value names particular expansions and finishes alongside rarity, foil and effects, so a first edition and a full-art border are each handled as their own case.
The pictures beside this entry are the game's own: the first-edition border, the icon for the later expansion, and the card icon it prints at its top rarity.

What this entry does not tell you: how many cards sit in each expansion, the odds of pulling a particular finish, or what any finish is worth. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Cards are grouped into a fixed list of named expansions.
The expansion list is the game's own fixed set of set names rather than a free label you can invent.
facts.evidence: identifiers: Tetramon, Destiny, Ghost, Megabot, FantasyRPG, CatJob, FoodieGO, Ascension

facts.claim: A card's finish is a separate fixed list of border styles.
facts.evidence: identifiers: ECardBorderType, CardBorder_Base, CardBorder_FirstEdition, CardBorder_Silver, CardBorder_Gold, CardBorder_EX

facts.claim: The game ships a border image for each finish, including the full-art frames.
Expansions and finishes are named among the things that move a card's price.
facts.evidence: identifiers: EPriceChangeType, ExpansionTetramon, FirstEdition, FullArtBorder, Foil

facts.claim: The game ships a card icon for its top rarity alongside the expansion and border artwork.
